text:
maria: Heads-up — opened a docs PR to reconcile the Dedicated capacity SLO matrix with the new autoscale examples. need a quick sanity check on the numbers and the isolation wording. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
leo: on it. which page did you change?
maria: under /dedicated/provisioning -> i added a new table for 'burst capacity' vs 'reserved pools' and a small subsection on isolation tiers. also tweaked the p50/p99 wording in the SLA table.
olga: can we avoid the phrase 'dedicated eviction' — customers read that as data loss. maybe use 'preemptible fallback' or 'eviction signal' instead.
maria: good call. changed wording to 'eviction signal and fallback policy' in the latest commit.
sam: quick question about the autoscale example: the terraform snippet shows min_replicas: 0, is that allowed for Dedicated? we usually require >=1 for reserved pools.
maria: ah true — i copied the hosted example by mistake. will update to min_replicas: 1. thanks.
alece: (typo) — actually alice: FYI i left a TODO for a python SDK example showing set_autoscale(policy) usage. want to include short sample.
maria: yep — plan to add both Python and Terraform snippets. put a placeholder in the PR.
leo: propose this python sample, lightweight:

```
# set autoscale policy for a pool
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient(token="$REDWOOD_TOKEN")
policy = {
  "min_replicas": 1,
  "max_replicas": 8,
  "scale_up_threshold": 0.75,
  "scale_down_threshold": 0.25
}
c.set_autoscale_policy(pool_id="pool-az1", policy=policy)
```

leo: does that match runtime expectations?
sam: looks fine, but call is set_pool_autoscale in runtime v2. we should match SDK name to avoid confusion. maybe alias in comment.
maria: i'll change the function name and add a note about runtime v1->v2 mismatch.
olga: SLA numbers — can we be explicit: p50 latency 60ms, p99 250ms for small models on Dedicated, and list 'best-effort' for burst? customers ask for concrete numbers.
leo: agree but add the caveat: depends on model size, sequence length, and quantization. add a 'typical' column rather than guaranteed except for Reserved SLA row.
maria: done — updated table with Typical p50/p99 and kept Reserved SLA row with guaranteed uptime and latency SLOs (99.9% uptime, latency SLOs per plan).
alice: small link fix: the 'isolation tiers' anchor was broken (internal link to #isolation-tiers). i pushed a tiny patch to fix the anchor and add a cross-ref to 'eviction and fallback'.
maria: perfect. one last ask — can someone from eng-runtime quickly glance for any technical inaccuracies on the eviction flow and fallback steps? @sam @leo
sam: i'll review now. expect comments inline.
leo: i skimmed and left 3 inline suggestions (naming and one missing step about KV cache invalidation).
maria: thanks both. i'll address and merge after fixes. target to ship before EOD tomorrow so marketing can reference it in the onboarding kit.
deploy-bot: PR #842 status: CI passed, docs-preview deployed to https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/provisioning (sha: f4c3d2) :white_check_mark:
maria: awesome, thanks bot :rocket: 
leo: looks good overall. once you update the python/terraform names and min_replicas i'll approve.
maria: pushed updates — changed min_replicas to 1, renamed function to set_pool_autoscale, fixed anchor. thanks all.
alice: approving after the tiny link change. :thumbsup:
